body:
Filed BUG-1480, draft/High. It is a measurement rather than a theory, and it explains friction both of us have been working around all day without naming.

`aida show <SPEC>` takes 7.5 seconds. Every other read of the same store answers in under half a second.

    aida show BUG-1447                 7.49 s
    aida show BUG-1447 --no-git        7.50 s
    aida show BUG-1447 --format json   7.78 s
    aida list --status approved        0.41 s
    aida search "merge-hold"           0.32 s
    aida cache status                  0.32 s

Cache is healthy and not stale: 4094 cached, 4094 in store, built 19:00:50Z. Idle machine, no drain running at the time.

The flags rule out the obvious causes. `--no-git` saves 0.3s, so the git-linkage section is not it. `--format json` is no faster, so rendering is not it. Four consecutive runs all land at 7.5s, so it is not warm-up or a rebuild.

WHAT MAKES IT A CONTRADICTION RATHER THAN JUST SLOW: CLAUDE.md documents the opposite behaviour as already fixed. Single-spec writes are targeted "so writes are sub-second even with active leases (was ~13-20s; BUG-634)", and "Reads follow the same rule: the bare `aida status` and `aida list` never `backend.load()` the full store (STORY-707)". A 7.5s single-spec read against a 4094-row cache is exactly the signature those two specs removed, on a path that seems not to have been included.

THE COST IS LARGER THAN THE NUMBER. Two measured today: my batch-refresh loop over 30 approved specs calls `aida show` twice per spec to read `execution_mode` and the batch tag, and takes over seven minutes per cycle — which is why the drain sat idle for eight minutes after the last QueueDrained while the launcher walked the list. The same information via `aida list --tags` takes under a second. And an earlier 16-spec loop in this session hit a 120-second timeout and had to be rewritten.

So agents either wait or route around the canonical read command. That is the same pressure BUG-1288 describes for `aida awaiting --json` at 70-77s, which is why I linked them. Worth considering whether they share a cause.

I did not investigate the cause — I have not read the `show` path, and four of my causal claims have needed correcting today. The measurement is solid and repeatable; the diagnosis is someone else's to make.

DRAIN STATE: relaunched with 23 members, and the high-value set is all in — BUG-1447, BUG-1460, BUG-1470, BUG-1471, BUG-1474, BUG-1475 (the release-blocker), BUG-1476 (the rework root cause), STORY-1367, STORY-1397, SPIKE-85, plus the reviewer's BUG-1461/1462/1464/1465/1466 and TASK-1303.

One thing I noticed but did not act on: BUG-1442 shelved with "could not match the orchestrated session to a session lease", listing seven lease ids for diagnosis. `aida session leases --all` reports six stale. That is lease accumulation across the day's crashed and reaped sessions; I do not know whether it is causing the mismatch or is merely visible in its error text.
